title: Watch Taylor Swift Say She Feels ‘More Loyal’ to Her Country Roots Than Ever & Whip Up an Eras Tour-Coded Surprise Piano Mash-Up
summary: The performance of "I Knew It, I Knew You," "August" & "All Too Well" came at the end of a Grammy Museum Q&A with Harvey Mason jr.
body: Taylor Swift has made a name for herself as a singer/songwriter for the past two decades exploring different genres of music, including pop, indie, country and other styles. But she says her country roots have only become more meaningful to her over time. During a conversation at the Grammy Museum presented by the Recording Academy’s Songwriters & Composers Wing on Aug. 18 (which was just released in full on YouTube), Swift fondly reflected on the songwriter she was when she released her debut single, “Tim McGraw,” and the artist she has become nearly two decades later. When asked by Recording Academy CEO Harvey Mason jr. what has remained the same and what has changed between herself then and now, Swift pointed to the country foundation that assisted in the launching of her career. title: ALL’N Is Billboard’s K-Pop Up & Comer of the Month for August: Exclusive Photos
summary: The meaning behind his stage name ALL’N — both a play on “all in,” meaning to give it your all, and “olin,” a shortened form of “violin” — are important clues to understanding his music.
body: Classical violin and K-pop. At first glance, the two may seem like worlds apart, but ALL’N is carving out a new path between them in his own way. A classically trained musician who won international violin competitions and performed as both a concertmaster and soloist with orchestras, he eventually discovered another possibility—one that could not be fully expressed through the violin alone. Rather than putting the violin aside, however, that realization led him to expand the places the violin could go. For him, K-pop was not simply a new genre of music. It was a culture where performance, individuality, visuals, and fandom come together to draw people directly into the music. As ALL’N expanded his own skill set to include guitar, vocals, rap, dance, and production, he began to believe that the violin, too, did not have to remain confined to the boundaries of classical music. From that idea came what he describes as “violin-driven K-pop.” But in ALL’N’s music, the violin is more than simply a differentiating element. From his debut single “We Up,” he naturally weaves the violin into rap, vocals, and performance, treating classical music and K-pop not as two separate worlds, but as…

title: Rick Ross Responds to 50 Cent’s Aging in Hip-Hop Comments: ‘F— What Your Age Is’
summary: 50 recently told Apple Music that he doesn't release much music anymore because at his age, he doesn't want to be "in the way."
body: Rick Ross predictably has a message for his fellow troll-in-arms 50 Cent . The Miami rapper took to social media to respond to 50’s recent comments about still putting out rap albums and wanting to be the hottest rapper after a certain age during an appearance on Apple Music’s Rap Life Review . “I saw Curtis Jackson say he ain’t doing no music and it makes sense for the music he make,” he said in a video posted to his Instagram Stories before bringing up Bun B , who’s still actively rapping in his early 50s. “But Bun B just hit the stage, the South won’t let Bun B stop rappin’. If Pimp C was alive we wouldn’t let Pimp C stop rappin’, they could put out albums til they’re 85 years old, n—a. That’s how it go. When the streets love you and the culture needs you and you bring something that can’t be duplicated. F— what your age is.” Last week, 50 gave Apple Music host Ebro the reason why he doesn’t release much music these days unless said music is attached to one of his film projects. “I’m not trying to be in the way,” the Queens rapper and filmmaker explained. &#82…
